title: BMP complex evaluation and acceptance protocol
scope: Reference-free assessment of candidate ligand–type-I–type-II ectodomain assemblies. This is a proposed workflow, not a validated confidence estimator. Numeric acceptance thresholds remain unset until benchmark calibration.
primary_instruction: Separate rewarded-contact satisfaction from independent support. Report every receptor copy and interface, including the weakest one. Missing evidence is unknown, not a pass or a failure.

stages.name: Biological target and construct
actions: Confirm ligand, receptor identities, mature sequences, modeled domains, stoichiometry and sequence-to-reference mapping.
Record evidence that this ligand–receptor combination binds or signals, separately from evidence identifying the pose.
Mark combinatorial targets without binding evidence as exploratory; do not assume every enumerated combination forms a stable complex.
Document mutations, glycans, tethering, disulfides and terminal-group assumptions.
stages.output: Target definition and biological evidence record.

stages.name: Evidence allocation
actions: For every experimental datum record its source, construct, assay, uncertainty and what it constrains: binding existence, residue involvement, local contact, orientation or assembly.
Label use as guidance, tuning, ranking, held-out evaluation or contextual information.
A datum used to tune weights or choose models is no longer held-out evaluation evidence.
Structural contacts and energetic mutation effects are different observations; mutation interpretation must consider folding and expression effects.
stages.output: Evidence ledger; explicit list of genuinely held-out observations.

stages.name: Reference-backed calibration
actions: Benchmark using experimental assemblies and interfaces with compatible constructs; label homologous or mutant references as surrogate comparisons.
Include generated incorrect poses and alternative orientations, especially plausible ones satisfying the rewarded contacts. Easy clash-heavy decoys alone are insufficient.
Use reference DockQ to label benchmark accuracy, and test how well the reference-free criteria distinguish successful and unsuccessful models.
Separate calibration and evaluation targets or interface families where feasible. Tune no threshold on the unknown target's eventual reference.
Document model training/template exposure where known; withholding coordinates from guidance alone does not establish a training-blind test.
Freeze thresholds, preparation, ranking and compute budgets after calibration. Report uncertainty from the small benchmark panel.
stages.output: Versioned calibration profile with thresholds and observed false-positive/false-negative behavior.

stages.name: Physical plausibility
actions: Run all-atom contact and geometry validation with documented hydrogen placement and protonation.
Inspect clashes, packing, hydrogen-bond geometry, unsatisfied buried polar groups, backbone and rotamer outliers, fold preservation and native disulfides.
Report whole-assembly metrics and local/interface outliers before and after refinement.
Use calibrated rejection criteria for severe geometry failures; physical plausibility alone never establishes the correct docking pose.
Keep energetically plausible rankings as model-dependent evidence; do not equate model energy with measured affinity.
stages.output: Physical checks: pass, fail or unassessed, with metric values and calibration profile.

stages.name: Independent runs and perturbations
actions: Use separately initialized FK populations with distinct random seeds. Log ancestry/resampling information when available.
Treat population descendants as correlated samples; summarize recovery at the independently initialized run level.
Sweep plausible noise settings and perturb uncertain guidance weights or remove selected restraints. Keep other inputs controlled.
Cluster arrangements after aligning the ligand and allowing valid identical-chain permutations; compare receptor orientations and interface contact patterns.
Record best and alternative clusters recovered by each independent run, rather than treating particle counts as independent confirmations.
Report recurrence and sensitivity as robustness diagnostics, not calibrated probabilities of correctness.
stages.output: Run-level cluster recovery and sensitivity table.

stages.name: Independent support and alternatives
actions: Evaluate held-out experiments separately from guidance satisfaction.
Distinguish agreement with a related interface from target-specific evidence.
Retain substantially different plausible arrangements when independent evidence does not discriminate among them.
Identify one or more measurable contacts or experiments whose predicted outcomes differ between alternatives; include appropriate folding or expression controls for mutations.
If evidence conflicts, investigate construct, assay, mapping and model assumptions before forcing compliance.
stages.output: Per-interface support level, unresolved alternatives and a discriminating observation.

stages.name: Acceptance and transfer
actions: Assign the output labels below per interface and for the assembly. Do not average away an unsupported or failed receptor interface.
Preserve candidates and alternative clusters with provenance. Do not label a reference-free structure experimentally solved.
Transfer newly predicted contacts as hypotheses with uncertainty; never relabel them experimental evidence.
An uncalibrated screen can produce provisional candidates but cannot award a calibrated acceptance status.
stages.output: Acceptance record and eligible transferable hypotheses.

result_labels.label: rejected_or_needs_repair
result_labels.definition: Fails a calibrated severe physical check or conflicts with reliable evidence after contextual review.
result_labels.next_action: Repair preparation or model; revisit inconsistent assumptions. Do not propagate its contacts.

result_labels.label: plausible_candidate
result_labels.definition: Passes calibrated physical checks, but independent pose-specific support is absent or insufficient.
result_labels.next_action: Retain candidate ensemble and seek discriminating evidence.

result_labels.label: supported_prediction
result_labels.definition: Passes calibrated physical checks; has positive, independent support at the stated structural scale; robustness has been assessed and alternatives are documented.
result_labels.next_action: Use for hypothesis generation and cautious transfer; state which geometry is supported and what remains uncertain.

separate_reference_comparison.note: If a suitable experimental reference exists, report reference-based accuracy alongside the support label. A partial reference validates only covered regions/interfaces; a homologous or mutant reference measures similarity to that surrogate.

implementation_notes: Use explicit null/unknown/unassessed values; no numeric zero for missing data.
No universal DockQ-equivalent threshold exists for the reference-free checks in this proposed protocol.
Independent validation means independence from this project's guidance, tuning and selection; experimental sources and model training may still be correlated.
A robust wrong restraint can reproducibly produce a wrong pose. Sensitivity checks therefore complement, rather than replace, independent evidence.

A practical first pilot is a small reference-backed panel with multiple independent restarts, several plausible noise settings and matched guided/unguided compute. Choose replicate counts after observing variability.
Keep a structurally precise claim, for example: type-I interface supported; type-II placement remains ambiguous.
Do not force all target combinations through a complete assembly requirement when biological binding itself is uncertain.

sources.name: DockQ official implementation
sources.supports: DockQ compares model and native structures; reports per-interface scores and chain mappings.

sources.name: Chen et al. 2010, MolProbity
sources.supports: Hydrogen-dependent all-atom contact, clash and stereochemical validation.

attribution: The operational calibration, evidence-allocation and acceptance workflow is a methodological recommendation for this project, not an established universal BMP validation standard.
